A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from DYNCL to DCL. All 25 pages of v1 and 38 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations and quantitative evaluations of linear, switching-linear and Lorenz dynamics, including ablations, held-out tests and additional metric analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds partial-observability and control experiments, analysis of mouse neural recordings, and evaluations of additional baseline methods.

M1.justification: The contrastive objective and switching-dynamics mechanism remain, but Appendix H adds consecutive or subsampled time-delay inputs for non-injective observations. Appendix I extends the learned dynamics with observed control inputs and a trainable control matrix B. These substantially extend the procedure beyond v1's implemented autonomous, single-time-step formulation; the DYNCL-to-DCL rename itself is cosmetic.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates synthetic systems only. V2 adds Allen mouse calcium-imaging recordings, rank-deficient observation scenarios, and systems driven by step-function or LDS control inputs (Appendices H–J). Appendix M also evaluates baseline reproduction on the TDRL 'changing' setting. The original synthetic coverage remains.

E2.justification: Table 8 newly evaluates TCL-B, PCL-B, PCL-L, TDRL-B and TDRL-L against DCL on SLDS data. TCL and PCL were discussed but not evaluated in v1. Existing identity/CEBRA-time, oracle and asymmetric-encoder comparisons are retained; CEBRA-time is not a newly added comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5 revises stated encoder widths from 512 units to dimension-dependent 30d/10d widths, changes Lorenz batch size from 2048 to 1024, and changes LDS/Lorenz negative counts from 32,768 to 20,000. These are reported setting revisions, without establishing reruns. V2 also changes the LDS alignment calculation and introduces neural-data train/validation splits and consistency evaluation, MCC evaluation, and baseline-specific budgets and checkpoint-selection rules.

E4.justification: New analyses test observation rank, time-window length and sparse lag selection (Figure 14), inclusion versus omission of control inputs (Table 4), neural embedding dimensionality, prediction offset and temporal shuffling (Appendix J), and component-wise versus linear recovery (Appendix L). V1's synthetic ablations, held-out tests and multistep dynamics controls remain.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains mean±standard-deviation reporting across three datasets and three repeats, with five datasets for Lorenz. Appendix H newly specifies 95% confidence intervals over nine dataset/model-seed runs. Appendices J and M specify five-run procedures for new experiments. There is no stated increase in repeats for the retained main results.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial control, partial-observability, neural-data and baseline results. For example, Table 8 reports low-noise R² of 99.52% for DCL+SLDS versus 91.33% for PCL-B. Table 1 changes the displayed LDS-model error from 0.38±0.34 to 0.77±1.07 under a new ×10^-2 heading. Revised metrics/settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting improvement. Tables 2–3 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and its main proof are essentially retained. Appendix H adds substantive time-delay observation-matrix and accumulated-noise derivations addressing non-injective observations; Corollary 1's justification and the LDS metric definition are also revised. The new observability argument is overbroad: full-rank A alone does not ensure a full-rank observation stack, since A=I preserves rank(C). A complete noisy-extension proof is explicitly deferred.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions paragraph and conclusion retain the central claims about identifiable contrastive recovery of latent dynamics and switching-linear approximation of nonlinear dynamics. The novelty claim for an identifiable, end-to-end, non-generative inference algorithm remains. The new appendix evidence does not substantially redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of Gaussian-noise and injectivity assumptions, partial observability, control-input interpretation, and neural embedding consistency. Appendices L–M explain linear versus component-wise identifiability and qualifications arising from different baseline assumptions. The exclusively synthetic limitation is revised to acknowledge the neural application. The warning that Lorenz dynamics recovery falls short was already present in v1.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit Apache 2.0 code-availability statement, whereas v1 already supplied a code link. It newly documents training-step counts, dynamics-specific learning rates, post-hoc baseline fitting, neural dataset access identifiers, and baseline adaptation details. Appendix K adds per-experiment compute accounting and runtime explanations, substantially expanding reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against nonlinear ICA and temporal causal representation learning in Section 7 and Appendices C, L and M. It distinguishes explicit dynamics estimation from demixing and causal-graph discovery, discusses comparator assumptions, and adds an AnInfoNCE connection. Most earlier references and the original contrastive-learning positioning remain.

P1.justification: The eight main sections and original appendices retain their order and much of their prose. Changes include DYNCL-to-DCL renaming, noise/control terminology cleanup, localized explanatory rewrites, corrected cross-references, author-year citations, a reproducibility statement and an appendix contents page. The established narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 14–17 and Tables 4–8, providing substantial new visual coverage of partial observability, controls, neural recordings, compute and baseline comparisons. Figure 1 removes the data-generation panel and changes placement; Figures 2 and 7 move. Table 1 gains revised headers, a scale annotation, expanded caption and theoretical qualifications. Most earlier experimental plots are retained.

improvement.justification: V1's validation was entirely synthetic and largely used internal model variants. V2 adds verified external baselines and a held-out neural-data study with shuffle controls, alongside partial-observability/control tests and substantially better implementation documentation. These address important gaps in comparative evidence and applicability. Neural consistency remains a proxy for identification, and Appendix H overstates what invertible dynamics guarantee about observability, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical validation and reproducibility.
